visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A middle-aged man with short black hair and glasses, wearing a black button-down shirt, stands in front of a digital background. He is holding a small black device, likely a remote or clicker, in his right hand. The background is a vibrant, green-dominated scene from a video game resembling Animal Crossing, featuring a pumpkin patch and a small white avatar standing nearby. The man is speaking directly to the camera with an expressive face, often gesturing with his hands to emphasize his points. (2) The screen transitions to a split view. The top half features a large, colorful text overlay on a white background with vegetable icons, stating "雙北房地產 血汗真相!". The bottom half shows a screenshot of a scientific research paper titled "Heat stress and productivity losses in urban construction workforces," published in Nature Cities. This phase serves as the introduction of the specific topic being discussed. (3) The view returns to the man in the black shirt in the same studio setting. He continues his animated narration, using his hands to point at the screen or the remote. His facial expressions are lively, showing surprise or concern as he relays data. The lighting is bright and even, highlighting his features against the colorful, blurred-motion-like game background. (4) A brief cutaway shows a close-up of a real person, a male construction worker, outdoors. He wears a dark green utility vest over a black shirt and a white hard hat. He looks weary, squinting slightly in what appears to be bright sunlight, and he uses his hand to adjust his hat, as if wiping sweat from his forehead. The background is slightly out of focus, showing structural elements of a construction site. (5) The camera returns to the host in the studio. He is now presenting various data charts that appear as overlays. One chart shows scattered black data points on a purple-to-pink gradient background, labeled "Light," "Medium," and "Heavy" workloads. He points towards these graphical representations as he explains the impact of heat on different types of labor. The visual rhythm is fast, with frequent cuts between the host and graphical data.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Slogan]: 超級細菌來襲?挺健康揭真相. [Variety]: 雙北房地產 血汗真相! [Subtitle]: 但真的不能再 HOT 下去了. (2) [Subtitle]: 中研院與勞動部聯手哈佛大學. (3) [Subtitle]: 在《Nature Cities》上 發表的研究竟然顯示. (4) [Subtitle]: 在臺北蓋房子 做工的人體感溫度會飆到 50.9 度 C. (5) [Subtitle]: 50.9 度不是氣溫 還不是. (6) [Subtitle]: 而是加了濕度的體感溫度. (7) [Subtitle]: 這個數值是美國國家氣象局認證的 危險等級. (8) [Subtitle]: 再上去一點點的 52 度 就是「極度危險」. (9) [Subtitle]: 中暑機率極高. (10) [Subtitle]: 不過體感溫度也不能表達他們有多熱. (11) [Subtitle]: 在工地門口指揮交通 跟在西曬鷹架上 感受肯定不一樣. (12) [Subtitle]: 只看氣象報告不準 拿溫度計去戳勞工朋友的... (13) [Subtitle]: 也不禮貌 所以科學家直接去問工人 旁邊的空氣. (14) [Subtitle]: 他們找了雙北 10 個工地的 101 位工人. (15) [Subtitle]: 在他們身上掛了一個「隨身感測器」. (16) [Subtitle]: 這玩意兒每分每秒都記下「現在到底有多熱有多濕」. (17) [Subtitle]: 提供超高解析度的「體感」數據. (18) [Subtitle]: 結果顯示 工人在工作時的平均體感溫度為 45 度 C. (19) [Subtitle]: 而最熱的時間點 欸 不是中午. (20) [Subtitle]: 而是傍晚五點 平均飆到 50.9 度 C. (21) [Subtitle]: 原來在工地裡曬了一整天的鋼筋水泥. (22) [Subtitle]: 傍晚正在瘋狂散熱 工地成了「旋風烤箱」. (23) [Subtitle]: 太陽跟熱氣雙面夾擊 工人無處可逃. (24) [Subtitle]: 科學家也把時間一秒一秒地拉出來分析. (25) [Subtitle]: 發現工人有 38.6% 的時間 都處在「危險」等級下工作. (26) [Subtitle]: 而另外 21.5% 的時間 是在「極度危險」等級. (27) [Subtitle]: 重點來了 光是因為太熱 工人的「生產力損失」. (28) [Subtitle]: 就高達 35.5% 等於工作三小時 就有一小時熱到沒辦法做事. (29) [Subtitle]: 科學家不是靠攝影監看 而是用國際公認的. (30) [Subtitle]: 「生理工作能力模型」(Physical Work Capacity, PWC). (31) [Subtitle]: 把人的心臟當成引擎 設定了安全轉速上限. (32) [Subtitle]: 每分鐘心跳 130 下. (33) [Subtitle]: 先前在實驗室裡已證明 環境溫度越高. (34) [Subtitle]: 為了不讓心跳爆衝超過 130 下 身體會「強制降速」. (35) [Subtitle]: 研究團隊把工人身上的每分鐘熱指數代入公式一算. (36) [Subtitle]: 發現在高溫下 為了保命、不讓心臟過熱. (37) [Subtitle]: 工人的身體機能被物理強制限縮了 35.5%. (38) [Subtitle]: 這不是偷懶 是生物本能在警告 「不要啊！再做下去斑紋要出現啦！」. (39) [Subtitle]: 但整篇研究最反直覺的 是做粗活搬鋼筋的「重度勞動」工人. (40) [Subtitle]: 損失的勞動力反而最少 損失最嚴重達 41.3% 的. (41) [Subtitle]: 卻是「輕度勞動」的工人 其次是中度勞動的 39.7%. (42) [Subtitle]: 重度勞動反而只有 29%. (43) [Subtitle]: 科學家推測這是「自我調節」的差異. (44) [Subtitle]: 也就是做粗活的更明白自己體力消耗快 會找地方躲一躲、喘口氣. (45) [Subtitle]: 反而「輕度勞動」的工人 可能被困在某個超熱的定點. (46) [Subtitle]: 像是焊接工 旁邊都是發熱的機器 只能一直被文火慢燉. (47) [Subtitle]: 這研究以血汗數據顯示 工人的熱傷害風險被嚴重低估. (48) [Subtitle]: 工人的體溫比房價更快「漲停」. (49) [Subtitle]: 如果你是有良心的房地產大老闆 記得送我一棟房子.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video serves as a science communication segment, aimed at explaining a specific research study about the extreme heat stress faced by construction workers in Taipei and New Taipei City. By synthesizing visual data charts and energetic narration, the host reveals surprising findings: that heat index at construction sites can reach dangerous levels, especially in the late afternoon, and that "light labor" workers might actually suffer more productivity loss due to constant exposure compared to "heavy labor" workers who self-regulate. The intent is to raise awareness about labor conditions and heat-related health risks through a data-driven, yet accessible and humorous, storytelling approach.
